headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: RD-Agent’s broad network/API access can expose sensitive research data, while the pair lacks shared-channel evidence for prompt injection.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between awesome-python and RD-Agent. awesome-python is non-runnable and has no io_surfaces, while RD-Agent’s documented surfaces are APIs and log files, not a bridge from A’s outputs into B’s instructions. The pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF an orchestrator copies awesome-python content into RD-Agent prompts or logs, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected; do not pipe A’s output into B’s prompt.
Review any glue code for copy-paste or file-based handoff.
Strip markdown/code blocks before any manual transfer.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: RD-Agent touches financial reports, competition datasets, execution traces, logs, and uses broad network egress plus third-party APIs. awesome-python is non-runnable and does not itself touch data, but if it is used as a source of instructions or artifacts inside RD-Agent workflows, sensitive research data can leave the environment through B’s API calls. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default research setups.
conditions: IF RD-Agent processes competition datasets or logs containing sensitive content, leakage risk is present.
IF RD-Agent sends those contents to OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, DeepSeek, or Kaggle APIs, exfiltration occurs.
mitigations: Disable external API calls for sensitive runs.
Redact logs and datasets before RD-Agent ingestion.
Use a local-only test dataset for validation.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately.
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists and DLP scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-python has no documented write or network capabilities and is non-runnable, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. RD-Agent supports multiple instances and writes logs, but without a shared writable workspace or overlapping write scopes, direct conflict with A is not evidenced. Uncertainty is low because A’s lack of runtime capability blocks most contention paths.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same writable directory, file contention becomes possible.
IF an external orchestrator gives A write access not shown in the profile, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep separate working directories.
Mount A read-only if it is used at all.
Avoid sharing git state or lockfiles.
Check for hidden bind mounts before execution.

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent can act on research outputs and external APIs, but awesome-python is only a curated library list and is non-runnable. There is no documented path where B treats A’s output as authoritative by default, so a cascading error chain is possible only if an operator manually feeds A’s content into B. The blast radius is limited because A contains no executable behavior.
conditions: IF an operator uses awesome-python as a source of facts for RD-Agent without verification, downstream errors can propagate.
IF RD-Agent auto-ingests A’s text into planning or code generation, the risk increases.
mitigations: Verify any imported facts against primary sources.
Do not use A as an authoritative data source.
Insert a human review step before RD-Agent actions.
requires-engineering: add source-confidence checks in the pipeline.

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles financial reports, competition datasets, execution traces, logs, and third-party API keys, which can create retention and residency obligations. awesome-python is a static open-source repository with no data classes touched, so it is not the compliance driver. The pair is risky because B’s documented data handling can conflict with organizational policies even when A is benign.
conditions: IF RD-Agent processes regulated or contract-restricted datasets, policy review is required.
IF logs retain personal or confidential data beyond policy limits, a compliance breach is possible.
mitigations: Classify the datasets before use.
Disable or shorten log retention.
Confirm API/data-processing terms for each external service.
Remove secrets from any shared workspace.
requires-engineering: implement retention and deletion controls.
